summary.prose: This Story builds the review pipeline every review runs through: a new module holding the delivered review job grown into a generic prepare, review and gather engine, one job per review unit (each code-review dimension, or one design review). It routes the code review and both kinds of design review through it with single-chunk adapters that send exactly today's prompts, now wrapped so each answer echoes its call's identifier, and makes the pipeline the only place a review call is retried. It adds the 128K-token chunk setting, recognises size refusals in reviewer sessions, and gives Ollama a read-only reviewer session so a high-end local model can run every review kind.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A new shared module, the review pipeline (proposed at src/workflow/review-pipeline), owns the three stages for every review. It is a serialisable job: the daemon drives it to the end; the controller is handed its calls one frame at a time and answers them by call identifier. Prepare measures material at 3 characters per token against review.chunkTokens (default 128,000 tokens); at or under the limit it emits one chunk whose prompt is the adapter's current single-call prompt, otherwise it groups the adapter's atoms by the adapter's relations and packs whole groups into chunks that each fit, adding a short summary of each related atom held in another chunk. Review issues one call per chunk serially; every call carries a fresh UUID that the answer must echo inside an envelope, an answer whose identifier is missing or wrong is rejected and retried under a new UUID, and a size refusal re-divides the chunk instead of resending it. Gather passes a single chunk's answer through unchanged and otherwise applies the adapter's gather rules (keyed obligations judged on all chunks' evidence, cross-chunk relationships, cross-chunk duplicates), each gather call itself bounded by the chunk limit. ISSUE-aef82b03's delivered InputTooLargeError, LLMProvider.inputBudgetChars, packIntoBatches and ReviewJob loop are moved under the pipeline as its core. A review kind is a series of stages, each a model stage or a deterministic one, preserving today's execution exactly: code review runs one stage per dimension exactly as today on each path: on the daemon, adherence (no call at all when there is neither an approved LLD nor an approved plan), conventions, coverage, quality and functional coverage are model calls, ux is deterministic and provider-free, and diagram keeps its registered handlers (some deterministic, such as the component handler) with today's per-handler isolation, a failing handler still recorded as a LOW observation; on the controller path the ux and diagram prompts are offered to the controller as today; HLD/LLD template review is one reviewer-session stage; DEF/plan premise review is extract (model), probe (deterministic) and verify, where the daemon path verifies one premise per call and the controller path verifies every premise in one batched call, as each does today; an adapter therefore declares its stage plan per path (daemon or controller). A review under the limit therefore makes exactly today's calls in today's order. Each call names its execution mode: a structured call run in the repository as its working directory (as today's code-review judges pass subject.repoPath; for the premise review's verify calls, which pass no working directory today, this is an additive change), each with its own per-call time limit where it has one today (the premise verify call keeps its 3-minute VERIFY_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS from ISSUE-d4b2cd1c), or a read-only reviewer session with the repository as working directory, the review's remaining deadline and its cancellation signal. Ollama gains a reviewer session through a generic read-only tool loop extracted from the analyzer's runShaperToolLoop, taking caller-supplied messages, answer schema, deadline, signal and retry policy, while the analyzer keeps its own wrapper unchanged. The pipeline owns every retry of a review call: every provider is called with internalRetry: false (CliProvider's transient retry and reviewer-session retry, and both providers' structured-output retry, make exactly one attempt), and the pipeline re-issues a transient failure, a stall, an invalid answer or an identifier mismatch once, under a new UUID: two attempts in all per call. Failure policy is per stage: a cancelled review always ends at once; a premise-review verify call that fails both attempts records that premise as not judged (MED, never a pass) and keeps the rest, as ISSUE-d4b2cd1c delivered; a diagram handler failure stays a LOW observation, as today; any other failed call (premise extraction included) fails the review and records nothing, as today. Gather is bounded at every step: an obligation's evidence (notes from every chunk, each keyed by the obligation and carrying the atom ids it stands for) is packed into the final adjudication call when it fits the limit; when it does not, it is reduced level by level, each reduction call reading one batch of that key's evidence and returning one note of at most a quarter of the limit under the same key, the job keeping which atoms and earlier notes each note stands for, until the key's evidence fits one adjudication call; a gather call refused for its size is re-planned like a chunk. Scope of the identifier and limit rules (stakeholder decision 2026-10-19 [[c14]]): they apply to every request the pipeline sends. A reviewer session's internal tool turns belong to the session, as they already do inside the claude and codex CLIs, where insrc cannot see them; the Ollama session's tool loop is likewise not identified or measured per turn. Every call records which material it carries (its chunk, atom ids and evidence-note ids), and the job keeps an immutable snapshot of the review's material taken once at prepare: for code review, today's grounding snapshot (the controller step already saves subject and grounding) plus every fact a deterministic stage reads from disk today, recorded at prepare (the ux stage's companion-mock existence checks); for design review, the document text and, for the premise review, the extracted claims and their gathered evidence. The adapter is rebuilt on every turn from the saved subject plus that snapshot and never re-queries the code graph or the files, so a refused call is re-divided from exactly the material it carried and a controller review resumes on the same material. A controller reports a call it could not complete as a failure outcome keyed by the call's identifier (size refusal with the reported limit, stall, transient error), which the driver handles exactly as a daemon-side failure: a size refusal re-divides the call, the others are re-issued once under a new identifier.

nonFunctional.performance: Calls are serial (k6). A review under the limit makes the same number of calls as today. Every prompt sent, chunk or gather, is at most review.chunkTokens x 3 characters.
nonFunctional.security: No new transport: calls go through the existing LLMProvider and the installed CLIs (k7). Reviewer sessions keep their read-only tool sets.

New record fields (pipelineCalls) are optional, under a new name, and absent on one-chunk reviews; the existing parts field keeps its shape; so existing records keep validating.

api.name: createReviewJob
api.signature: createReviewJob(adapter: ReviewAdapter<unknown>, path: 'daemon' | 'controller', snapshot: ReviewMaterialSnapshot, limitChars: number): ReviewPipelineJob

parameters.name: adapter
parameters.purpose: The review unit's adapter (sc2): its material, per-path stages and gather rules.

parameters.name: path
parameters.purpose: Selects the adapter's stage plan for this path.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.purpose: The immutable material taken at prepare; never re-queried afterwards.

parameters.name: limitChars
parameters.purpose: review.chunkTokens x REVIEW_CHARS_PER_TOKEN.

returns.meaning: Prepare's result: the chunk plan (single when the material fits the limit) and the first stage's pending calls, each enveloped with a fresh callId.

errors.condition: One atom alone exceeds the limit; names it. Never cut.

preconditions: The snapshot was taken by the adapter's own prepare step from the review's subject.
postconditions: Under the limit, the first stage's calls carry exactly today's messages and schema inside the envelope.
Every pending call has a callId no call of this job carried before.

Grouping order over the limit: prepare first unites atoms joined by 'calls' relations, then 'same-file', then 'same-module', then 'references'. It packs whole groups into chunks that fit, and a group too large for one chunk is split along the next-weaker relation kind before single atoms are placed. Relation direction does not matter for grouping. Atoms keep the material's order within a chunk.

Divided with no atoms: when the single call (the adapter's singleCalls rendered with all its context) is over the limit, the job is divided even if the material has zero atoms, for example a diff review whose coverage has no symbols but a large test record. Prepare plans no chunk calls. Every obligation goes straight to gather and is judged by obligationCall on its own context atoms, packed by the s1 packer so that every call fits. An obligation context atom that alone does not fit raises AtomTooLargeError naming it.
single: true is set only when the rendered single call fits the limit; an empty material does not by itself mean single.

Sizing (amended 2026-10-20): a candidate group is measured with the summaries it must carry, those of usage-related atoms outside it ('calls', 'references'); proximity summaries ('same-file', 'same-module') are added afterwards while they fit the packing budget. So grouping related atoms together never fails merely because of optional context lines.

Obligation context (amended 2026-10-20, user decision): GatherPlan.obligationCall(key, evidence, context) receives the obligation's own context atoms (the material.context entries its atomIds name). When the obligation's call does not fit the limit, each of its context atoms becomes an evidence note under its key, once (job.contextReduced), and is reduced with the evidence level by level under the note cap; the obligation is then judged on the notes, whose provenance names every context atom. Nothing is dropped. A context atom too large for one reduction call alone raises AtomTooLargeError naming it ('context atom <label>').

Gather validation and refusal (amended 2026-10-20 after review): every gather answer (obligation, relation, reduction) is checked against its schema and then the optional GatherPlan.validate(answer, call); a non-empty result is the 'invalid-answer' failure, re-issued once with the reasons, then the review fails. A refused obligation call that carried raw context converts that context to notes (as at sizing) and re-divides the notes and the converted context, so nothing it carried is lost and later planning does not reattach the context.

api.name: runReviewJob
api.signature: runReviewJob(job: ReviewPipelineJob, adapter: ReviewAdapter<unknown>, provider: LLMProvider, opts: { readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined }): Promise<unknown>

parameters.name: job
parameters.purpose: The prepared job.

parameters.name: adapter
parameters.purpose: Rebuilt from the subject plus the job's snapshot.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.purpose: Called with internalRetry: false for every call.

parameters.name: opts.signal
parameters.purpose: Cancels the review at once.

returns.type: unknown (the adapter's result R: DimensionResult or ReviewReport)
returns.meaning: The serial daemon driver: issues pending calls one at a time, runs deterministic stages, validates each enveloped answer, re-issues a failed call once under a new callId, applies each stage's failure policy, gathers, and returns the adapter's finished result. R per adapter (amended 2026-10-20 after review): a code-review dimension's R is its DimensionResult (an object, which carries pipelineCalls when divided); a design review's R is its findings array (readonly Finding[]), left an array, and runReview / runTemplateReview read the calls per role from the finished job (opts.onDone with pipelineCallsOf(job)) into ReviewReport.pipelineCalls.

errors.condition: The signal fired. It is checked before every call and after every answer, and it is passed into the call in flight, so the provider ends that call at once (the CLI's process group is killed; the Ollama request is aborted). Nothing is retried or recorded.
A call in a 'fail-review' stage failed both attempts; the review fails and records nothing, as today.
Re-division after a size refusal reached one atom that does not fit.

postconditions: No prompt hash is issued twice.
A 'record-not-judged' stage keeps every other judgement and records the failed one as not judged (MED); a 'record-observation' stage records a LOW observation.
Cancellation ends the review at once, including a call in flight: the provider throws AbortError within moments of the signal, never after the call's own time limit.

api.name: ReviewPipelineDriver.nextCalls / applyOutput / applyAnswer / applyFailure / result
api.signature: nextCalls(job, adapter, now?): readonly ReviewCall[]; applyOutput(job, adapter, callId, raw, now?): ReviewPipelineJob; applyAnswer(job, adapter, answer: EnvelopedAnswer, now?): ReviewPipelineJob; applyFailure(job, adapter, callId, cause, maxChars?, more?): ReviewPipelineJob; result<R>(job): R

parameters.name: callId (applyOutput)
parameters.purpose: The id of the call the caller sent: the EXPECTED id, supplied by the caller (the daemon driver knows which call it made; the controller step names the call each answer is for). It is never read from the model's answer.

parameters.name: raw (applyOutput)
parameters.purpose: The model's raw output, expected to be the envelope { callId, answer }. Its echoed callId is compared with the expected one: missing or different is the 'identifier-mismatch' failure (re-issued once under a new callId, then the stage's policy); equal goes on to applyAnswer with the inner answer.

parameters.name: answer
parameters.purpose: { callId, answer }: an answer already matched to its call. applyAnswer checks the answer against the stage schema and the stage's validate (an invalid answer is the 'invalid-answer' failure); it does not check an echoed id. It rejects a callId that is not a pending call's.

parameters.name: cause
parameters.purpose: Why the call did not complete.

parameters.name: maxChars
parameters.purpose: The size a refusal reported, when it did.

returns.meaning: The pure step functions both runReviewJob and the controller step (s5) drive.

errors.condition: applyAnswer for an unknown callId, or applyAnswer/applyFailure on a finished job.

preconditions: The adapter is the one the job was prepared with, rebuilt from the same subject and snapshot.
postconditions: A size refusal re-plans the call's carried atoms and notes within the reported (else halved) budget; transient, stall, identifier-mismatch and invalid-answer re-issue once under a new callId.

Which to call (amended 2026-10-20 after review round 2): a model's raw output goes through applyOutput, which owns the echo check; applyAnswer is for an answer already matched to its call. The daemon driver uses applyOutput; the controller step (s5) uses applyOutput for each answer it is handed, naming the call the answer is for.

errorCases.scenario: A model answer whose callId is missing or differs from the call's.
errorCases.detection: applyOutput compares the enveloped answer's echoed callId with the expected id of the call it answers, before schema validation.
errorCases.response: The answer is discarded and the call re-issued once under a new callId; a second mismatch applies the stage's failure policy.
errorCases.userImpact: None when the re-issue succeeds; otherwise the stage's policy (fail, not judged, or observation).

errorCases.scenario: An answer whose inner answer fails the adapter schema.
errorCases.detection: validateAgainstSchema on the envelope's answer field after the callId check, then the stage's optional validate (for the template review, validateTemplateAnswer).
errorCases.response: Re-issued once under a new callId with the validation errors as the correction note; then the stage's failure policy. When the correction would not fit the limit, it is left out (never shortened) and the omission is logged; the re-issue is otherwise the same.

errorCases.scenario: The provider refuses the prompt for its size (completeStructured, claude session envelope, codex session).
errorCases.detection: InputTooLargeError: from completeStructured as today, from the codex session as today (runCodex's sizeRefusalOr), and newly from the claude session's is_error envelope.
errorCases.response: applyFailure re-plans the call's carried atoms within the reported maxChars less the retry reserve (else half the refused prompt); never resent. Under the limit with a single unsplittable atom: AtomTooLargeError naming it.
errorCases.userImpact: More calls; a review that fits nothing names the item.

errorCases.scenario: A transient CLI error or a stalled codex session (CliStallError).
errorCases.detection: The provider, called with internalRetry: false, throws on its first attempt.
errorCases.response: Re-issued once under a new callId; then the stage's failure policy.

errorCases.scenario: A verify call fails both attempts in a DEF/plan review.
errorCases.response: That premise is recorded as a MED 'not judged' finding with its cause; every other premise is kept and the review is stamped (ISSUE-d4b2cd1c).
errorCases.userImpact: The review blocks under the default policy but is recorded.

errorCases.response: A LOW observation is recorded, as judgeDiagram does today.

errorCases.scenario: Premise extraction, a code-review model dimension or the template session fails both attempts.
errorCases.response: The review fails and records nothing; runCodeReview returns { ok: false, error } as today. Only the attempt count changes: two attempts in all (pipeline policy) instead of today's nested retries.

errorCases.detection: The AbortSignal fires. It is checked before every call and after every answer, and it is passed into the call in flight: runInProcessGroup kills the CLI's process group, and the Ollama request's fetch is aborted.
errorCases.response: AbortError at once, even mid-call. The call is not retried, and nothing is recorded (no not-judged recording).
errorCases.userImpact: Better than today: a cancel no longer waits for the in-flight call's time limit.

errorCases.scenario: The template review is configured on a provider with no runReviewSession.
errorCases.detection: The reviewer-session execution mode finds no runReviewSession on the provider.
errorCases.response: The review fails with today's message naming the provider requirement; with Ollama it now has one.
errorCases.userImpact: Only providers that are neither CLI nor Ollama.

errorCases.scenario: The template review's time limit passes, possibly during a re-issue.
errorCases.detection: Before issuing, the driver compares now with job.deadlineAt; a session call already running is bounded by deadlineMs = deadlineAt - now.
errorCases.response: ReviewSessionTimeoutError; no further call; the review fails with today's message and records nothing.
errorCases.userImpact: As today: one limit for the whole review.

errorCases.scenario: An Ollama reviewer session is cancelled mid tool loop.
errorCases.detection: The signal reaches the in-flight complete or completeStructured request and is checked before each turn and tool run.
errorCases.response: AbortError at once; no further turn; nothing recorded.
errorCases.userImpact: The cancel takes effect within the turn in flight.

errorCases.scenario: An Ollama reviewer session's model returns a call to a tool it was not offered (for example file_write).
errorCases.detection: The generic tool loop checks the call's name, after alias resolution, against the allowlist before dispatch.
errorCases.response: The call is not executed. The model gets a tool error ('not available in this session'), the refusal is logged, and the loop continues within its turn budget.
errorCases.userImpact: A review can never write to the repository.

errorCases.scenario: An obligation's evidence cannot shrink: every note is within the note cap, yet no two fit one reduction call, so a level would reduce each note alone.
errorCases.detection: requestNoteCall finds every planned reduction batch holds one note and every note is within noteCapChars.
errorCases.response: Error 'the evidence for <key> cannot be reduced to fit one call (<n> notes)'; the review fails and records nothing (runCodeReview returns { ok: false }, a design review throws), never a partial verdict.
errorCases.userImpact: Raise review.chunkTokens (a larger limit lets notes share a reduction) or lower the noteCapChars the adapter sets, and run the review again.

errorCases.scenario: An obligation's evidence still does not fit one call after MAX_GATHER_LEVELS (16) reduction levels.
errorCases.detection: requestNoteCall counts levels per key (job.gatherLevels) before planning another.
errorCases.response: Error 'the evidence for <key> did not fit one call after 16 reduction levels'; the review fails and records nothing.
errorCases.userImpact: In practice unreachable (each level at least halves the notes); if seen, raise review.chunkTokens and run the review again.

migration.stateBefore: Delivery note (2026-10-20): this section and the steps below describe the code as it was before Story s1 was built; s1's build (tasks t1-t13) delivered them, so the review pipeline, the provider options, the Ollama reviewer session and review.chunkTokens now exist. The 2026-10-20 amendment changes only prepare's neighbour-summary rule, extraction's working directory and deterministic-stage cancellation. Each review path builds and sends its own calls (s1 analyze bundles). runCodeReview (src/workflow/code-review/runner.ts:171) runs each dimension through its own withStructuredRetry wrapper (3 attempts, e.g. src/workflow/code-review/dimensions/adherence.ts:155). runReview (src/workflow/review/review.ts:108) runs extractClaims (src/workflow/review/extract.ts:166), then a probe, then verifyClaim (src/workflow/review/verify.ts:214) for each premise; it routes HLD/LLD to runTemplateReview (src/workflow/review/template-review.ts:50), which calls CliProvider.runReviewSession (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:420). Providers retry inside the call: CliProvider.withTransientRetry (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:251) makes 3 attempts and OllamaProvider.completeStructured (src/agent/providers/ollama.ts:537) uses withStructuredRetry (src/agent/providers/structured-output.ts:186). No call carries an identifier. The ISSUE-aef82b03 ReviewJob and packIntoBatches live under src/workflow/code-review (review-job.ts:210, :321; pack-into-batches.ts:34). There is no review.* config key. In reviewer sessions, a codex size refusal is already classified as InputTooLargeError (runCodex, src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:566), but a claude is_error envelope throws a plain Error (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:448). OllamaProvider has no runReviewSession, and the analyzer's tool loop is private to src/analyze/context/driver.ts:863.
migration.stateAfter: One module, src/workflow/review-pipeline, holds ReviewPipelineJob, the pure driver step functions, the serial runReviewJob driver, packIntoBatches and the single-chunk adapters for every code-review dimension, the premise review and the template review. runCodeReview, runReview and runTemplateReview keep their signatures and result shapes, and route every model call through the pipeline. Each call is wrapped in the identifier envelope, sent with internalRetry: false, and re-issued at most once under a new callId by the pipeline. review.chunkTokens (default 128000; x3 = 384,000 chars) sets the limit. Size refusals from reviewer sessions surface as InputTooLargeError. OllamaProvider implements runReviewSession over a generic read-only tool loop that runShaperToolLoop also uses. Under the limit, every review makes today's calls in today's order and gives today's results.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional internalRetry field to StructuredCompletionOpts and ReviewSessionOpts, and signal to ReviewSessionOpts. Add an optional attempts parameter to CliProvider.withTransientRetry, set to 1 when internalRetry is false. Map internalRetry false to maxAttempts 1 in OllamaProvider.completeStructured. When the field is absent, behaviour is unchanged.

Classify size refusals in the claude session's is_error envelope as InputTooLargeError in CliProvider.runReviewSession, using the classifier completeStructured already uses. The codex session is already classified through runCodex; keep it and add a regression test.

Add an optional signal to ProcessGroupOpts (kill the group on abort, report aborted). Forward StructuredCompletionOpts.signal and ReviewSessionOpts.signal through runSubprocess in CliProvider, and through a per-call fetch in OllamaProvider, so that an abort ends the call in flight with AbortError, never retried. Absent signal: unchanged.

Extract the generic read-only tool loop and final structured emit from runShaperToolLoop behind caller-supplied messages, schema, deadline, signal and retry policy. Repoint both production callers at it unchanged: runShaperToolLoop and runShaper's legacy tail (src/analyze/context/driver.ts:539) (existing analyzer tests are the guard). Add the optional runReviewSession to the LLMProvider interface and implement it on OllamaProvider over that loop.
Add the review.chunkTokens catalog entry (number, default 128000) and REVIEW_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3. Old config files without the key get the default through the existing config reconcile fill step.

Create src/workflow/review-pipeline. Move packIntoBatches and grow the delivered ReviewJob into ReviewPipelineJob, with the envelope, the driver step functions, the failure policies, refusal re-division, the bounded gather, and the deadline. The only consumers of the old review-job.ts API (createReviewJob(strategy, budget), runReviewJob(strategy, provider), DimensionStrategy, Atom, jobResult) are its own tests, src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/review-job.test.ts and src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/pack-into-batches.test.ts. They move with the module and are rewritten to the new API. review-job.ts is deleted, with no compatibility wrappers. pack-into-batches.ts keeps a re-export at its old path, because packIntoBatches is unchanged.

Add the single-chunk adapters, each wrapping its existing prompt builder unchanged: the code-review dimensions, the premise review (extract, probe, verify with record-not-judged and the 3-minute limit) and the template review (one reviewer-session stage). Each adapter has daemon and controller stage plans.

Switch runCodeReview, runReview and runTemplateReview to build a pipeline job per review unit and drive it with runReviewJob. The per-dimension withStructuredRetry wrappers and verifyOrRecord's own retry go off the review path. Add the optional pipelineCalls field to DimensionResult and ReviewReport, absent on single-chunk reviews. Parity tests on recorded answers are the guard.
Rebuild and update the installed daemon (maintenance.update) so that the MCP and the IDE plugins use the pipeline. No stored review record is rewritten.

migration.backwardCompat: The public entry points runCodeReview, runReview, runTemplateReview, verifyClaim, extractClaims and runShaperToolLoop keep their signatures and result shapes. Every new field (internalRetry, signal, attempts, pipelineCalls, LLMProvider.runReviewSession) is optional, and when absent behaviour is unchanged for callers outside the review path, including the companion assess call and the analyzer. Stored code-review and design-review records keep their shape: pipelineCalls is absent on single-chunk reviews, and DimensionResult.parts stays readable but is no longer written. The old ReviewJob API (createReviewJob(strategy, budget), runReviewJob(strategy, provider)) is not preserved: its only consumers are its own tests, which move and are rewritten. packIntoBatches keeps a re-export at its old path. The IPC and MCP payloads do not change, so the VS Code and JetBrains plugins need no change. The controller frames are unchanged until s5. ProcessGroupOpts.signal and ProcessGroupResult.aborted are optional; callers that pass no signal see no change.

alternativesConsidered.name: One pipeline job per review unit, grown from the delivered ReviewJob
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new src/workflow/review-pipeline module whose job (sc5) is the delivered ReviewJob generalised: one job per review unit (a code-review dimension, or a whole design review), driven by runReviewJob for the daemon and by nextCalls/applyAnswer/applyFailure for the controller.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The delivered review-job.ts, pack-into-batches.ts and their tests move under src/workflow/review-pipeline and are generalised in place: DimensionStrategy becomes the ReviewAdapter (sc2) with per-path stage plans; ReviewJob becomes ReviewPipelineJob (sc5) with the material snapshot, the per-call carries record and the issued-prompt hashes it already keeps; the existing whole/MAP planning becomes prepare's single-chunk and chunked planning (s1 ships the single-chunk path and the generic grouping; the code and document relations are s2's and s4's). The envelope (sc4) wraps every call's schema as { callId, answer } and the driver re-issues once under a new UUID. One job runs per review unit: each code-review dimension is its own job, as each dimension is its own call today; a design review is one job with its stages.

The entry points keep their signatures and call runReviewJob: runCodeReview drives one job per expected dimension in today's order; runReview drives the premise or template job. Providers gain internalRetry and runReviewSession becomes optional on LLMProvider; OllamaProvider implements it over a generic read-only tool loop extracted from runShaperToolLoop. review.chunkTokens joins the config catalog.
pros: Reuses the delivered and tested job core (planning, refusal re-planning, prompt-hash dedupe, merge) instead of writing a second one.
One job per dimension matches today's call structure exactly, so the single-chunk path reproduces today's calls with no regrouping.
The controller path (s5) can keep one job per dimension in step state, as the delivered design already planned.
cons: Moving review-job.ts and pack-into-batches.ts changes their import paths for the tests delivered under ISSUE-aef82b03.
Generalising DimensionStrategy into ReviewAdapter touches every place the delivered tests build a strategy.

constraintScore.notes: One job per dimension reproduces today's per-dimension calls exactly.
The delivered issued-prompt hashes plus the envelope give fresh identifiers and no repeated prompt.
The delivered refusal re-planning carries over.
Per-dimension job carries the HLD's dimension field.

alternativesConsidered.name: One pipeline job per whole review
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A single job holds every dimension (or every design-review stage) of one review, so prepare plans chunks once and every dimension reads the same chunks.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
ReviewPipelineJob covers the whole review: prepare measures all of the review's material once and plans one chunk set; every dimension's stage then issues its calls against those chunks. The driver walks dimensions in today's order inside the one job. The rest (envelope, retries, providers, config, Ollama session) is as a1.

This needs one material and one chunk plan per review, so the code-review adapter's material must be the union of every dimension's material, with per-dimension views on it.
pros: Chunks are planned once per review rather than once per dimension.
The controller holds one job per review instead of one per dimension.
cons: Dimensions read different material (adherence the approved design, coverage the test record, conventions the rules), so one shared chunk plan fits none of them well and forces a per-dimension view layer the HLD does not have.
Departs from the delivered ReviewJob, which is per dimension, so less of it is reused.

constraintScore.notes: Today's per-dimension calls need a view layer to reproduce.
Material becomes a union across dimensions.
The HLD job carries one dimension.

alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: One shared chunk plan does not fit dimensions that read different material; sc5's per-dimension job shape is strained.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How the serial daemon driver runs one review unit under the limit: prepare takes the snapshot and emits one chunk, each call is sent enveloped with internalRetry false, and a failed or mismatched answer is re-issued once under a new callId before the stage's failure policy applies.

messages.description: Pending calls, each with a fresh callId in the envelope schema.

messages.description: A mismatch or failure is re-issued once under a new callId; a size refusal re-divides the carried atoms; then the stage's failure policy applies.
